notes.text:
The proposed surface obstruction is valid for the ACTUAL G331 geometric C/D cone, over EVERY field k. It also has a stronger signed primary-model version and an exact canonical filtration. Put R=k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z)/(xy), a=m=(x,y,z), X=V_m, retaining ALL supports. This is a reduced excellent nonnormal surface. Its finite normalization is S=k[x,z]_(x,z) times k[y,z]_(y,z); R is the fibre product over k[z]_(z). Pairs have identical x=0,y=0 residues; subtracting their common residue shows R is generated by z and the separated x- and y-terms. The component idempotents make S finite. Testing multiplication by those idempotents shows its conductor is exactly c=(x,y). The reduced conductor quotients are k[z]_(z) and two copies of it. Their normalized boundary consists of two points over one point o: support(x,y), v_o(z)=1. G331 identifies precisely these two source points, with singleton fibres everywhere else.

On branch1, y=0, set f1=-1/2. On branch2, x=0, set f2(w)=-1/2-1/(2w(y)), with 1/infinity=0. Normalization gives min(w(y),w(z))=1, so w(y)>=1. Extended evaluation w(y) is continuous, and reciprocal on [1,infinity] is continuous and tends to0. Hence f2 is continuous, in[-1,-1/2]. Both source values at EVERY conductor fibre are -1/2. The compact finite quotient topology gives a genuine continuous signed function f downstairs. No unsupported claim that f is psh is made.

Let v1 be the branch2 GENERIC monomial valuation with y=z=1; x is killed. For ANY proper primary ideal I, e=v_o(I) is a positive finite integer. Choose an element attaining e and write it as a polynomial divided by a local unit. In its branch2 numerator the y=0 residue has a nonzero z^e coefficient. The generic monomial valuation has no cancellation between distinct monomials, so its total-degree minimum is<=e. The denominator has nonzero constant and value0 at both valuations. Thus v1(I)<=v_o(I). Unit ideals give equality0. Negative combinations consequently satisfy q(o)<=q(v1). G331's proved uniform comparison applies to the ENTIRE geometric C, including real Cartier core evaluations and uniform closure, so EVERY g in C satisfies g(o)<=g(v1). Taking infima in an ACTUAL decreasing C-net proves the same inequality for EVERY g in D, including bottom. This is the substantive geometric bridge; it uses a supplied comparison theorem, not a new ideal-defined cone.

Every C/D minorant of f therefore has g(o)<=f(v1)=-1. Moreover EVERY normalized semivaluation on the regular second branch dominates its ordinary m-order: polynomials in m^e have value>=e and units have value0. By the same uniform and decreasing bridge, g(w)<=g(v1) for ALL branch2 w. Thus every such minorant is<=-1 throughout branch2, including arbitrary supports.

For n>=1 let I_n=m^(2n)+x^2 m^n and h_n=-v(I_n)/(2n). This ideal is proper primary because it contains m^(2n) and is contained in m. Ideal sum/product identities hold on EVERY support. On branch1,
h_n=max(-1,-1/2-v(x)/n),
whereas on branch2 and at o it is identically-1. On ACTUAL Bl_(I_n), I_n O is invertible with a regular generator, defining effective Cartier E_n; -E_n/(2n) is negative effective REAL Cartier and relatively ample. Its degree is positive on EVERY contracted integral curve, before any limit is taken. Hence h_n is an actual geometric-core competitor. It is below f everywhere. On every branch1 point with finite x-value, h_n increases to-1/2; the sole branch1 point killing x is the conductor point. The constant-1 is also a competitor. The COMPLETE raw C/D supremum is consequently
p=-1/2 on branch1 minus o; p=-1 on branch2, including o.
The upper bound on branch1 is f1; the upper bound on branch2 was proved for every geometric competitor. This determines p on the entire boundary, not only on sampled monomial points.

Define branch1 w_r(x)=r,w_r(z)=1,w_r(y)=infinity, r>=1, by generic monomial minima. For each polynomial, as r tends to infinity its minimum tends to the order of its x=0 residue, or infinity if that residue is0. All local unit denominators have value0. Thus w_r converges pointwise on EVERY element of R to o. But p(w_r)=-1/2 and p(o)=-1. The raw supremum is not USC or continuous. Every D function is USC, being an infimum of continuous functions. A greatest C or D minorant would equal the respective raw supremum (the two agree by n1), so neither exists. Equivalently such a greatest minorant must dominate all h_n, take value-1/2 on the finite-x branch1 locus and<=-1 at o, contradicting USC. The USC regularization p* has p*(o)=-1/2, p*(v1)=-1; away from o the two component loci are open and p* equals p. It violates the geometric inequality. It remains<=f, but cannot be declared geometrically positive.

A finite signed primary-model obstacle has the SAME failure. Let J=(y)+m^2, an actual proper primary ideal, and F=(1/2)v(J)-(3/2)v(m). On X, branch1 gives F=-1/2; branch2 gives F=(1/2)min(w(y),2)-3/2 in[-1,-1/2]; F(o)=-1/2 and F(v1)=-1. This is a signed actual exceptional REAL Cartier evaluation on the directed common primary blowup of m and J. The SAME h_n are below F, and the SAME universal inequalities prove exactly the same raw p and no greatest C/D minorant. The failure already occurs for a signed model obstacle.

For BOTH f and F the canonical ideal in EVERY degree m>=1 is explicitly
A_m=(z^m)+x(x,z)^(ceil(m/2)-1)+y(y,z)^(m-1).
Indeed on branch1 its requirement is equivalent to ordinary order>=ceil(m/2), by the generic order valuation and domination by all normalized supports. On branch2 the requirement is equivalent to order>=m: necessity is v1, sufficiency follows from f2,F2>=-1. A pair with these orders belongs to R precisely when its common z-residue has order>=m. Separate the common residue and its x- and y-divisible remainders to obtain the displayed ideal, including arbitrary local-unit denominators. Thus on branch1, writing s=v(x),t=v(z), min(s,t)=1,
h_m=-min(mt,s+ceil(m/2)-1)/m;
on branch2 and at o, h_m=-1. This is an all-support ideal identity, not an experimentally inferred filtration.

All h_m have actual negative effective ample primary presentations, and converge pointwise in EVERY degree to p. Nevertheless ||p-h_m||_infinity=1/2 for EVERY m: choose t=1 and finite s>=m-ceil(m/2)+1 to get h_m=-1,p=-1/2; elsewhere the difference lies in[0,1/2]. The canonical algebra is not finitely generated, by n1's elementary forward implication from finite generation to a continuous rational-primary envelope. Here non-FG accompanies a proved failure; it is not the reason substituted for that failure.

The failure is stable on an open set of continuous obstacles. If ||f'-f||<epsilon<1/4, every h_n-epsilon is a geometric C minorant of f'. A greatest C/D minorant would therefore have values>=-1/2-epsilon on the finite-x first-component locus. At o the universal two-point inequality forces value<=f'(v1)<=-1+epsilon. USC along w_r would require the opposite lower bound -1/2-epsilon at o, impossible when2epsilon<1/2. This also shows that failure is not a single fragile equality case.

Homogeneity is explicit. On the unnormalized cone write lambda=v(m). The original branch2 obstacle is -lambda/2-lambda^2/(2v(y)), interpreted as- lambda/2 if v(y)=infinity; branch1 is-lambda/2. It is homogeneous of degree one. F already is a homogeneous signed ideal evaluation. The raw p is -lambda/2 on the finite-x first-component locus and-lambda otherwise. For a new primary gauge b divide the same homogeneous functions by v(b) and use G331's exact ray homeomorphism; bounded positive denominators preserve the discontinuity and the no-greatest conclusion. Canonical ideals remain identical under this transported obstacle. Completion also preserves the example.

This is a genuinely NONNORMAL envelope obstruction with a two-point infinite-conductor fibre. Each normal surface component individually has CE by n1. It contradicts neither the bijective-normalization theorem reconstructed in n1 nor reduced-curve min(f,0): curve conductors have finite value and no such identified boundary points. Literal classical/CLD radial profiles, products, energy and full finite-map operators remain separate. The new exact formulas require no new resolution, finite generation, F-finiteness or characteristic assumption. notes.detailedSummary: Actual conductor separators and G331 normal divisorial bounds produce a strictly negative continuous signed primary-model obstacle with no greatest C/D minorant. All-support divisorial density proves the USC contradiction. Requires a cross-component normalization fibre; no source CE or higher-dimensional resolution is assumed.
notes.text:
A general cross-component conductor obstruction follows from the ENTIRE qualified G331, without assuming that the normal components have CE. Let R be any excellent reduced positive-dimensional local ring, a a primary gauge, S its finite normalization, rho its FULL boundary quotient and c its conductor. Suppose one rho-fibre has lifts alpha,beta on normal local centres belonging to DIFFERENT minimal components of R. Then some bounded strictly negative continuous SIGNED PRIMARY-MODEL obstacle on R has neither a greatest geometric C nor a greatest geometric D minorant.

Choose a regular c0 in the conductor. The normalization has idempotents e1,e2 for the two distinct minimal-domain factors. Since the conductor is an S-ideal, j=c0 e1 and ell=c0 e2 belong to R. They vanish identically on every other component and are nonzero on their own domain factors. The nontrivial fibre lies on the infinite-conductor stratum by G331, so alpha,beta kill c0. These are actual elements downstairs, not hypothetical separated branch functions.

Choose a centred divisorial valuation nu on the normal local centre containing beta, normalized by aS. G331's normal-domain divisorial bound supplies a finite K>=1 such that nu(I)<=K beta(I) for every unit-or-primary ideal on this centre. Precisely, the nonunit bound nu(h)<=C ord_m(h), together with beta(m)>=1/r for m^r subset aS, gives nu(I)<=Cr beta(I); units are separate. Consequently every negative finite REAL primary combination satisfies u(nu)>=K u(beta). Uniform comparison and actual decreasing infima give this for ENTIRE geometric C and D. Pullback of a target g therefore yields g(rho(beta))<=g(rho(nu))/K. This uses exactly G331's normal bound, its actual cone comparison and full-support pullback. It introduces no analytic irreducibility claim for nonnormal R.

The number d=nu(ell)=nu(c0) is positive finite. Choose integers L>d and B>0 so that 1+B(1-d/L)>K. Put b=B+1 and the ACTUAL proper primary ideal I=(ell)+a^L. Define the homogeneous signed primary-model obstacle
F=(B/L)v(I)-(B+1)v(a).
On V_a it lies in[-b,-1]; on component1 it is exactly-1, and its value at the common fibre is-1. At rho(nu) it is -1-B(1-d/L)<-K. It is continuous by primary-ideal evaluation and is a signed REAL Cartier evaluation on a directed common primary blowup. Every geometric minorant g<=F therefore obeys g(rho(beta))<=F(rho(nu))/K<-1.

For every n>=1 put T_n=a^(bn)+(j)a^n and q_n=-v(T_n)/n. These are actual proper primary ideals. Their negative effective REAL Cartier divisors on ACTUAL Bl_(T_n) are relatively ample, hence have positive degree on EVERY contracted integral curve. On component1 the profile is max(-b,-1-v(j)/n), and on every other component it is-b. Thus q_n<=F on EVERY support. At each component1 point with finite j-value their supremum is-1. This locus is dense in the full component1 boundary: G331's all-support divisorial-density theorem gives a dense subset of generic-support centred divisorial valuations, and j is nonzero there. In particular alpha lies in its closure, even though alpha kills the conductor.

A greatest C or D minorant would dominate every q_n and thus equal-1 on this dense locus (F itself is-1 there). Its normalization pullback is USC. If its value at alpha were<-1, an open strict sublevel neighbourhood of alpha would meet the dense locus, a contradiction. But alpha and beta have the same target point, where EVERY minorant is strictly below-1 by the preceding inequality. Therefore no greatest C/D minorant exists. This is a proof using dense nets in general; no metrizability or sequence extraction is assumed.

An algebraic sufficient condition for the fibre hypothesis is that two distinct minimal primes p1,p2 satisfy dim R/(p1+p2)>=1. Take a centred semivaluation of the reduction of this excellent positive-dimensional quotient, whose boundary is nonempty by G331. Its support contains both primes. For each i its factor through R/p_i lifts by finite normalization lifting to a normal centre of the i-th normalization domain. These give two lifts in different components of the same full rho-fibre. Their conductor value must be infinite by uniqueness on the finite stratum. Hence EVERY such positive-dimensional intersection of distinct irreducible components obstructs the all-continuous-obstacle envelope property, in ANY dimension, characteristic or residue field. The produced obstacle is already a signed primary model.

This does not address nonsingleton fibres lying entirely within a single minimal-domain normalization, nor all excellent normal dimension>=3 envelopes. No arbitrary-model cofinality, resolution, degree averaging, source CE, newly defined ideal cone, or omitted conductor support is used. Every statement is gauge covariant: F and q_n are homogeneous, positive gauge transport divides by the same bounded denominator. The universal geometric obstruction is mathematical reasoning relative to G331, not a finite computation or an original-task closure.

notes.text:
There is an EXACT obstacle-by-obstacle existence criterion on the normal-crossing surfaces of n2, and a sharp universal CE criterion for excellent reduced surfaces with normal irreducible components. These are new scoped results, using ENTIRE qualified G331 and own n1--n3.
